title: A Shattered Asteroid May Have Bombarded Earth 800 Million Years Ago
hook: One asteroid shattering near a gravitational 'gateway' carved out by Jupiter may explain a wave of impact craters across the inner solar system — and a climate shakeup on Earth.
key_points: A catastrophic asteroid breakup may have triggered a wave of impacts ~800 million years ago.
The debris launched from near a gravitational 'gateway' controlled by Jupiter's gravity.
Fragments are thought to have struck Earth, the Moon, and Mars.
The bombardment may explain a cluster of ancient lunar craters.
It could also have contributed to major climate and biological changes on Earth.
content_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, a single catastrophic asteroid breakup roughly 800 million years ago may have set off a wave of impacts across the inner solar system. Researchers trace the debris to a spot near a gravitational "gateway" shaped by Jupiter's pull, which sent fragments raining toward Earth, the Moon, and Mars.
extra_html: The proposed bombardment offers a tidy explanation for a cluster of ancient lunar craters that has puzzled researchers, and it may have coincided with — and possibly contributed to — major climate and biological upheavals on Earth around the same time. It's a reminder that a single violent event far out in the solar system can echo across multiple worlds at once.

related.title: A Wobbling, Peanut-Shaped Asteroid Reshaped by Sunlight
related.hook: NASA's Lucy found that asteroid Donaldjohanson is a peanut-shaped relic of an ancient collision — slowly reshaped by sunlight, and still carrying traces of old water.
